062: Southern England 1355 summer afternoon. A sawyer yard suffering a bottleneck: enormous accumulated round logs but almost no finished square beams. STRICT nearly vertical bird's-eye view from directly above, ground fills entire image, no sky and no horizon. A long rectangular open sawpit at center with a log across it and two pit sawyers, one above and one below, plus a third carpenter waiting beside conspicuously EMPTY beam racks. Round logs arranged upper left, empty rectangular racks bottom right. Ordinary authentic hand tools. Do not use low eye-level diagonal log foreground.
067: Southern England 1360 autumn. Choosing ONE steward to take over two previously divided duties. Side-on view under an open manor arcade, two very distinct rival candidates seated at opposite ends of a long plain oak settle, a single large estate key-ring resting between them. Younger clean-shaven practical estate manager in faded blue with a wooden grain measure and soil-stained boots; older thin grey-haired accountant in subdued plum holding a bundle of tally sticks, looking toward the same single key-ring. They each extend one hand toward that sole key-ring, hesitant to claim the combined office. A small closed ledger is secondary beside the accountant, no displayed papers. Only these two figures, both faces visible. No lord's back in foreground, no laborers working, no coins changing hands, no carts. The tension is selection between practical estate knowledge and accounting ability, not paid work or rent relief.
068: Southern England 1360 summer. A completed building subsidy has been paid but the promise to fund future work remains open despite depleted finances. CLOSE oblique still life in an outdoor mason's work shelter beside a visibly finished new stone well: an open nearly EMPTY oak payment chest with only two coins; a matched pair of split tally sticks laid across its lip records payment already completed. Above the chest, a long blank parchment grant notice remains firmly fixed OPEN to a timber post with a large wax seal hanging from it. The steward's hands at far right try to close his empty purse while a mason's hand at far left points emphatically to the still-open sealed grant. Completed well visible background, no construction unfinished, no line of applicants, no market, no meadow or gate. No readable writing on grant. Important visual contrast: empty paid-out chest below versus still-valid grant pinned open above.
077: Southern England 1400 spring. A tiny request would establish a much larger common-land entitlement. VERY CLOSE view from grass level at a common meadow entrance: one tiny silver penny held between thumb and finger at extreme foreground left; beyond that hand the open five-bar wooden pasture gate leads into a huge open meadow occupied by grazing sheep and many distant cottage holders waiting with animals. A large old wax-sealed rolled parchment is tucked under the petitioner's other arm at the left edge, secondary and no writing visible. Gate and expanse occupy most of frame, coin intentionally minuscule yet readable. The lord's hand on the gate latch at right is hesitating, not collecting tax. No coin collection bowl, no rent sacks, no market stalls, no queue at a counter. Entitlement to an entire common meadow in exchange for a trivial request.
078: Southern England 1400 autumn. Two rival stewards argue opposite sources of relief: market-day money versus tenant rent. A wide frontal view of an OUTDOOR town-edge collection court with visibly distinct channels. At LEFT a prosperous merchant beside colorful folded wool cloth on a market stall has a few silver coins in a weighing pan; a blue-clad candidate pushes the coin pan back toward the merchant, advocating lower market dues. At RIGHT a coarse-clothed tenant brings a large grain rent sack and a wooden grain measure; a russet-clad second candidate lifts only a small measure from the sack and gestures to let the tenant keep the rest. Four people only, all faces visible. A low open fence separates the market side from the fields side. No lord observing from back, no carts being pushed, no person carrying another person's heavy load, no documents or table meeting. Two clearly contrasted financial relief proposals, cash from trade versus rent in grain.
